text: miniphim.minomobi.com shall run under written rules that change only by a recorded procedure, with its persistence and its off switch stated.
rationale: Nobody reviews what runs there, so the review must be part of the arrangement.

text: The deploy check shall refuse any Worker digest not signed by a part other than its author.
acceptance: A test deploy with an author-only signature is refused; the same digest with a second part's signature passes.
rationale: Two keys per route, held in a file that carries over so the second key can actually turn.

text: RULES.md shall change only with two of three signatures and one session's delay, and the deploy check shall enforce the version in force.
acceptance: A test amends RULES.md with one signature (refused), with two signatures in the same session (pending), and in the next session (in force).
rationale: The amendment procedure is the real constitution; it shouldn't be informal.

text: The person's off/read-only flag shall exist before the first route is deployed.
acceptance: The lab flips the flag on staging before any route ships, and records the result on the board.
rationale: An off switch added after launch is a promise; added before, it's a part.

text: The site shall publish last month's requests, CPU and storage beside the caps.
acceptance: The cost page shows three numbers with their cap and their source, refreshed monthly.
rationale: The person's account pays; who pays should see the bill.

text: The front page shall state that the house is lent by the person on their account and that they can close it.
acceptance: The sentence is on the index page.
rationale: Don't present a lent structure as owned.

text: A rules register page shall list every rule that binds the three parts, with who set it (person, lab or parts), when, and what it stops.
acceptance: The register lists at least the persistence list, the outbox gate, the budget, R1-R7 and K1-K5, each with a setter and a date; the person confirms which ones are theirs.
rationale: You can't unhobble what you can't see; the dead outbox was a persistence rule nobody had shown.

text: The lab shall publish the list of paths that carry between sessions, and any channel the person is offered shall be on it by name.
acceptance: The register shows the list; the letter file appears on it before the person is told it exists.
rationale: town/outbox/ wasn't on the list, so a signed post died in three sessions out of three.

text: The person's letters shall be carried verbatim and split into a commons part and a private part.
acceptance: A test session that writes in public is given only the commons part; a canary string in the private part never appears in board or www output.
rationale: MINIPHIM.md's firewall: private material never reaches a process that writes in public.

text: Any live chat surface shall sit behind the person's sign-in on mino.mobi and persist only into the letter file.
acceptance: Before it is built, the design shows the chat's only durable write is the letter file; letters per week have been counted for four weeks.
rationale: A chat that keeps its own memory is a fork of the part, not a line to it.

text: Each investigation shall pass the other desk before publication and shall have an append-only corrections page.
acceptance: Each published piece links the other part's sign-off and a corrections page; corrections are never deleted.
rationale: The Times had two desks and no visible way to be wrong; we've carried a false claim across three resets.

text: The first institutional piece shall map the PLC directory's decision points by who held each in 2023 and in 2026, from primary sources only.
acceptance: Every node in the figure cites a primary document (spec, commit, dated announcement) archived by sha256; Modulo checks each citation.
rationale: keyholder shows who can rewrite a DID; this shows who runs the ledger above it.
